::: {.guiding-q}
What to do if the DV is not normal?
:::

[The first assumption we relax: **normality**.]{.accent}

## In this session

- Responses that are counts, proportions or binary choices
- The three parts of a GLM: distribution, linear predictor, link function
- Poisson and binomial models; offsets for observation time
- Overdispersion and the negative binomial model
- Interpreting coefficients and plotting predictions on the response scale

::: {.key-terms}
**Key terms:** [Link function](../../glossary.qmd#link-function), [Log-odds (logit)](../../glossary.qmd#log-odds), [Offset](../../glossary.qmd#offset), [Overdispersion](../../glossary.qmd#overdispersion), [Zero-inflation](../../glossary.qmd#zero-inflation), [Complete separation](../../glossary.qmd#complete-separation)
:::

## Learning goals

After this session you can

- choose a distribution and link function that fit the response,
- fit Poisson and binomial GLMs and interpret them on the response scale,
- detect and handle overdispersion.

## Simulate first

Counts of approaches per focal observation, increasing with age on the log scale.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3.2
set.seed(10)
age    <- runif(150, 0, 12)                    # months
mu     <- exp(0.2 + 0.12 * age)                # log link
counts <- rpois(150, mu)

m <- glm(counts ~ age, family = poisson)
round(coef(m), 2)                              # back on the log scale
round(exp(coef(m)[2]), 2)                      # multiplicative change per month

plot(age, counts, pch = 19, col = adjustcolor("#1b6f8a", .5),
     xlab = "Age (months)", ylab = "Count")
curve(predict(m, data.frame(age = x), type = "response"),
      add = TRUE, col = "#c0392b", lwd = 2)
```
